subject: Private deployment: egress authentication, IP allowlist, and contract checklist

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the contract draft. Before we sign, our security team needs concrete answers on how Redwood's private connector behaves from an outbound/networking perspective. High level items we need confirmed and a checklist we can include in our internal approval packet: 

- Static egress IPs (are there stable source IPs we can allowlist?)
- Port & SNI expectations (will outbound be 443 only, do you expect SNI preservation?)
- TLS & client auth (support for mTLS or client certs from our side?)
- DNS resolution model (does Redwood resolve FQDNs on our side or yours?)
- NAT / ephemeral IP rotation cadence (if IPs are ephemeral, how often do they change and are rotations scheduled?)
- Connectivity fallbacks (if a given IP is blocked, does the control plane route to a different region/model?)

We have an SOC/controls packet to complete by 11/12. Can you provide a concise response we can attach (ideally a one-page checklist + short explanatory paragraphs)? Also can you attach any evidence you have for IP ownership/cert chains (we heard you can provide an attestation PDF).

Apologies for the many questions — our compliance folks are strict about outbound controls for private deployments.

Jordan
Security Ops, EuroHealth Systems

Hi Jordan — appreciate the list. Below is a concise checklist you can drop into your packet, followed by short clarifications and a pointer to the attestation we can share. If you'd like this formatted into a single-page PDF we can generate that after you confirm the account/region.

Required allowlist & egress expectations (EuroHealth — private connector / VPC deployment):
1) Source IPs: Redwood Private offers two modes: (a) Reserved static egress IPs — we can assign a small set of static IPv4 addresses per deployment (recommended for customers who need allowlist stability), or (b) Ephemeral NAT pool — shared across tenants in a region (not acceptable for strict allowlist controls). For contract sign-off we recommend reserved static egress IPs.
   - Action: Confirm "Reserved static egress" in SOW to procure IP assignment.
   - Evidence: IP custody attestation will be provided as a signed PDF (we attach a templated attestation).

2) Ports & protocol: Outbound connections from the private runtime to Redwood control-plane or model cache endpoints use TCP/443 (TLS1.2+). No other outbound ports are required by default.

3) SNI and FQDN: Redwood preserves SNI for routing. We publish the FQDNs you need to allow (e.g., controlplane.eu.redwood.ai, models-eu.redwood.ai). If you use an on-prem DNS sink, ensure those FQDNs resolve to the allowlisted IPs.

4) TLS / client authentication: Mutual TLS (mTLS) is supported for the control-plane handshake between your connector and our management endpoint. Data-plane model inference traffic uses server-terminated TLS; if you require client certs for outbound egress, we can enable outbound mTLS on a case-by-case basis (requires SOW and certificate exchange).

5) DNS resolution model: Redwood suggests split-horizon DNS where your environment resolves our published FQDNs to the reserved egress IPs. If your network prevents external DNS resolution, we support manual IP/SNI mapping in the connector config.

6) IP rotation & maintenance windows: Reserved static IPs are stable; we do not rotate them routinely. For security patches that require IP reallocation we will give a 30-day notice and coordinate a maintenance window. Ephemeral NAT pools rotate unpredictably and are unsuitable for allowlists.

7) Fallbacks & resiliency: Our runtime deploys multi-region failover but only to other Redwood-managed IPs in the same account region. If you allowlist only a single IP and we failover, service may be impacted. Recommended approach: allowlist the full set of assigned IPs (primary + standby) and the controlplane FQDN.

Checklist (one-paragraph summary for your packet):
Redwood Private (VPC) uses reserved static egress IPs when selected in the SOW. Outbound traffic is TLS 443 only; SNI is preserved and we publish the FQDNs. mTLS is available for control-plane handshakes; outbound data-plane may optionally be configured for mTLS on request. Reserved IPs are long-lived and subject to scheduled maintenance with 30 days notice. For failover, allowlist the full assigned set and published controlplane FQDNs. Redwood will provide an IP custody attestation PDF and a short network checklist for procurement.

Attachments we will send after signature:
- IP custody attestation (signed)
- Final allowlist text block (copy-paste for firewall teams)
- DocuSign link for the SOW (if legal requires explicit egress SLA)

Ben — adding you for commercial confirmation and to confirm whether SOW will include static IP add-on.

Thanks,
